title: Enclosure
summary: A case with a lid for a circuit board, with connector openings and mounting posts.

questions.label: Board name or model
questions.placeholder: e.g. Raspberry Pi 5, or a custom board
questions.why: A known board has an official mechanical drawing to read the dimensions from.

questions.label: Mounting hole spacing, long side
questions.why: Positions the posts; a wrong spacing means the board does not mount.

questions.label: Connectors that need openings
questions.placeholder: e.g. 2 x USB-A on the short side, USB-C power, HDMI
questions.why: Each opening needs its position and size from the board drawing.

questions.label: Cooling
questions.why: Heat decides the openings and may change the material.

questions.label: Lid
questions.why: Screws need inserts or bosses; a snap or press fit needs a test print.

load.note: Board weight; the board itself makes heat.

material.why: Holds its shape better than PLA near a warm board.
material.consider: PLA for a board that stays cool.

checks.name: Board and connector clearance
checks.why: The board drops in and every connector lines up with its opening.

checks.name: Lid fit
checks.why: The lid closes and stays closed; test the fit on a small piece first.

checks.name: Screwdriver access
checks.why: Every screw can be reached with a real screwdriver.

checks.name: Assembly order
checks.why: The board, cables and lid go together in an order that works.

checks.name: Ventilation
checks.why: The openings match the heat the board makes.
